projects.name: Powering Eswatini’s Delivery Engine: The Citizen‑Centred UniPod Total
projects.description:
The overarching objective of the UniPod project is to establish a vibrant and sustainable innovation hub at the university, designed to accelerate youth and graduate-led entrepreneurship. The project seeks to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and market application by providing innovators with access to technology, mentorship, and business development support. The project addresses structural barriers to innovation by creating a "one-stop shop" where young entrepreneurs can develop, prototype, and scale their ideas. It aims to foster a culture of innovation within the university, strengthen the national innovation ecosystem, and create meaningful employment opportunities for youth.
Expected results include:
•	An operational UniPod facility with digital fabrication tools and co-working spaces.
•	A robust pipeline of youth-led innovations and startups in strategic sectors.
•	Strengthened capacity of innovators in business management, intellectual property (IP) protection, and market readiness.
•	Formalized partnerships between the university, the private sector, and government agencies to support the innovation ecosystem.
•	An effective IP management framework, developed in collaboration with the host university and national IP authorities, to ensure innovators can protect and commercialize their creations.

projects.name: UNESCO_“Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa
projects.description:
The project “Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa”, a European Union project implemented by UNESCO, will contribute to strengthening the contribution of culture and heritage to sustainable development, notably through enhancing culture and heritage-based tourism development, diversifying tourism products and delivering high-quality visitor experiences at selected UNESCO-designated sites and cities. These activities aim to contribute to improving livelihoods of the communities in the region, including youth, women and indigenous peoples, through capacity building and the creation of opportunities for income-generation and jobs.

Through innovative partnerships, the project will invest in the development of engaging storytelling, the production of meaningful digital content and authentic, relevant products incorporating new narratives. It will enhance cultural production capacities to develop community-based programming and tourism offers at the participating UNESCO-designated sites and cities. At the same time, the project presents a unique occasion to promote international cooperation and peer-to-peer learning opportunities among the six target Southern African countries, namely Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, as well as with European Union countries, to foster regional integration and social cohesion.

children.name: By 2030, people in Eswatini are benefiting from efficient and resilient systems that deliver quality services, particularly for the vulnerable populations
children.description:
Between 2026 - 2030, the UN system in Eswatini, in close relationship with the Government and stakeholders, aims to deliver transformative development results that address the country's most pressing socio-economic challenges.
This outcome area seeks to strengthen the efficiency and resilience of systems to deliver quality services, particularly for the most vulnerable populations. This includes women, youth, PWD, PLHIV, key populations, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and children. The result reflects a commitment to strengthening public service delivery systems that are inclusive, shock-responsive, and rights-based. It supports progress across multiple SDGs, including health (SDG 3), education (SDG 4), gender equality (SDG 5), reduced inequalities (SDG 10), climate action (SDG 13), and peace, justice, and strong institutions (SDG 16). Through this outcome, the UNCT will help build a more equitable and resilient Eswatini, where no one is left behind and development gains are protected against future shocks.

children.description:
In Outcome 2 of the CF 2026-2030, the UN in Eswatini aims to foster an enabling environment for economic development, empowerment and livelihood diversification, contributing directly to poverty eradication and inclusive economic growth. This outcome supports the Government’s efforts to reduce
poverty (SDG 1), end hunger and achieve food security (SDG 2), and promote decent work and sustained economic growth (SDG 8). The UNCT will work with national institutions, the private sector, and civil society to strengthen value chains, enhance access to finance particularly for MSMEs and promote skills development aligned with market needs. These efforts will help unlock economic opportunities for vulnerable populations, including women, youth, and rural communities, ensuring that economic growth is both inclusive and sustainable.

children.name: Strengthened coordination among state and non-state institutions addressing disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, response and sustainable recovery
children.description:
**Number of multistakeholder coordination mechanisms established and active**

This indicator measures the number of formal multistakeholder coordination mechanisms that have been established and are actively functioning to strengthen collaboration, information sharing, joint planning, and coordinated decision-making among relevant stakeholders. These mechanisms may include disaster risk reduction (DRR) platforms, emergency response committees, coordination forums, working groups, and other sectoral or inter-agency structures. The indicator assesses the extent to which such mechanisms are operational and contribute to effective preparedness, response, risk management, and coordinated action among government institutions, civil society, development partners, communities, and other relevant stakeholders.

children.name: Governments capacity  strengthened to increase efficiency in domestic financial resource mobilization, management, as well as accessing external financing
children.description: This indicator measures the extent to which government capacity has been strengthened to improve the efficient mobilization, management, and use of financial resources, as well as access to external sources of financing. It captures improvements in areas such as revenue generation, public financial management, budgeting, expenditure control, financial planning, resource allocation, and systems for accessing development assistance and other external financing. The indicator reflects progress in enabling governments to mobilize and manage resources more effectively, transparently, and sustainably in support of national development priorities.
